tone.quote: Accentuation of words is by stress in Penutian, but has been too irregularly recorded to make its representation throughout this paper worth while. Accent is commonest on the penult and antepenult, but extends from the last to the fourth from the last syllable ... In Costanoan, stems of two syllables prevail. But antepenultimate accent occurs, most formative, locative, and modo-temporal suffixes being added to the root without causing a shift of accent. In fact, there is no certain case of any Costanoan word being accented other than on the first syllable of its stem.
tone.locator: pp. 84 and 88-89, section 'Accent' (Penutian chapter); Costanoan sources and dialect abbreviations pp. 55-56 of the same paper
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: No tone system described. Word accent = stress (dynamic), 'too irregularly recorded'; in Costanoan the accent sits on the first syllable of the stem and formative/locative/modo-temporal suffixes do not move it (so antepenultimate accent arises in suffixed words). Statement is for Costanoan as a family from six mission varieties; Karkin unsampled; its own 34-item 1821 list carries no accent marks…
